newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians see worse economic conditions now - poll.
newsitem.headline: Australians see worse economic conditions now - poll.

text.p: Most Australians believe they are economically worse off now than during the height of the last recession in 1990/91, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.

The Sydney Morning Herald's AGB-McNair poll found almost 50 percent of 2,000 voters surveyed believed that unemployment was higher now than five years ago, even though the latest rate was actually down more than two percentage points to 8.7 percent.
The newspaper said the results showed that any good news in the government's 1997/98 budget would be lost on the vast majority of Australians.
Treasurer Peter Costello was due to release the budget for the year to June 30, 1998, at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT) on Tuesday.
"The results confirm that perceptions about the state of the economy remain pessimistic, despite the big reduction in unemployment and interest rates since the recession," the paper said.
"Australians seem to know little about overall economic performance, and what they believe is generally bleaker than reality."
The poll found 43 percent of the voters surveyed believed that the budget deficit was larger in 1997 than in 1992.
The latest estimate actually has the deficit at A$8.5 billion for the 1996/97 year, down from A$17 billion in 1992.
On the interest rate front, 17 percent believed rates were higher now and nine percent believed they were the same.
In addition, 75 percent of those surveyed said the gap between rich and poor had grown over the past 20 years.
